data.role_evolution_summary: The aerospace engineering intern role is shifting from manual drafting and simulation setup to co-designing with AI tools. You're now expected to work alongside generative design software and AI-driven CFD platforms, making system-level thinking and AI fluency as important as classical fundamentals. For flight systems and mechanical analysis, routine tasks like telemetry processing, mesh generation, and first-pass FEA are being automated, freeing you to focus on higher-level interpretation and validation.

task_shifts.changing: Topology optimization in Siemens NX or ANSYS that used to require manual iterative CAD work is now handled by AI, proposing multiple structurally optimized geometries automatically.
task_shifts.meaning: Your engineering judgment to select and refine AI-generated designs—knowing why one topology works over another—becomes your key differentiator.

task_shifts.changing: AI surrogate models and agentic AI accelerate or replace many standard simulation runs, delivering predictions 10–100× faster than traditional solvers.
task_shifts.meaning: Your ability to interpret and validate AI outputs—spotting when a result is physically implausible—matters more than manually clicking through setups.
task_shifts.task: Setting up and running routine CFD simulations

task_shifts.changing: Processing test data, creating dashboards, and generating routine reports are now automated by AI analytics tools.
task_shifts.meaning: Your capacity to ask the right questions of the data and communicate insights clearly to engineers and managers becomes the value you add.

task_shifts.changing: AI-driven automation flags common issues before human review, so you spend less time checking standard specs and more on edge cases.
